data.summary: Execute configured JavaScript in the engine's isolated code-node runtime.

requiredFields.note: The script, run as the body of an async function (await works). Required. An empty script runs nothing and the node succeeds; a script that does not parse fails the node.

optionalFields.note: Optional free-text note about the script. No effect on execution.

Optional DLP settings. With isDlpEnabled and at least one rule, the $utils.logger entries in the node's execution log are scrubbed. $memory, $context and the error message are not.
The name the author gives the node, e.g. 'Preguntar datos al usuario'. Every node type accepts it. A label only. No effect on execution.
Per-node non-happy-path handlers. Absent: the workspace handlers apply. Present, even empty: they replace the workspace handlers for this node.
Handler the engine runs when this node fails with no edge to follow. The only entry it looks up on non-conditional nodes.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.

Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.

One tracking event: its name, when it fires, an on/off switch and the payload fields.

false keeps the event configured but never emits it.
When the event fires: 'always' (default when absent), 'success' on a successful run, 'error' on a failed one.

Copy of the node's free-text comments. No effect on execution.
Copy of the id of a workflow the node was stored in. The node belongs to the workflow that stores it. No effect on execution.

outletDocs.description: The script finished without throwing: its $memory writes and deletes are saved and its $context changes are kept for the next nodes.
outletDocs.fires: When the script returns, an empty content included (nothing runs). Every success edge fires, in stored order; none wired ends the run cleanly.

branches.when: Optional: a CODE node may be the last one. Write the branch as 'success', never 'default'.

outletDocs.description: The script threw or did not parse. None of its $memory set / setJson / delete calls is saved and its $context changes are dropped; a setFile already written stays.
outletDocs.fires: When the node returns an error. Every failed edge fires, in stored order. None wired: nonHappyPathHandlers.error answers if set, else the workspace error handler.

branches.when: Optional. Never wire it to END: a non-empty failed branch disables both error-handler fallbacks and swallows the error.

notes: The sandbox has no console, fetch, require or import, and the script runs under a 2 s timeout. Globals: $memory, $context, $input, $output, $env, $secret, $user, $bot, $company, $message, $webhook and $utils.{dayjs, _, shortly, uuid, crypto, logger}. Use $utils.logger.log(key, value) — it keeps 5 entries and truncates each value at 5000 chars — and an HTTP node for network calls.

Reading a let/const before its declaration in the same scope is a blocking error (CODE_USE_BEFORE_DECLARE): the wrapper is an async function, so it throws "Cannot access 'x' before initialization" at runtime. A reference from inside a nested function is fine.

Sandbox globals are accessors, not plain objects: write $user.get('id') and $context.get('key'). A direct property read such as $user.id is a blocking error, and execution metadata is not guaranteed to be present in $context.

$output.set() / $output.get() are rejected in a workflows/*.json graph — a plain workflow declares no outputs, so the runtime throws 'Key <key> not found'. Inside tools/*.json they are exactly how a CODE node returns a value.

Memory v2 surface: get(key, default?) primitives, getJson(key, defaultJson?) objects, getFile, set(key, value, TTL?) primitives-only, setJson(key, value, TTL) with TTL required, await setFile(key, base64, TTL, mime), delete(key | [keys]); setFile with a PDF mime is a blocking error (CODE_PDF_GENERATION) — PDFs come from the document-pdf Function. FileHandle: .toUrl() sync, await .toBase64()/.toRaw(). Mixing get and getJson on the same key throws, a key containing a dot throws, and get on a missing key with no default throws 'Key <key> not found'.
Limits: string ≤ 1024 chars, number ≤ 15 digits, JSON ≤ 15 KB with a TTL of at most 86,400 s (1 day), file ≤ 10 MB with a TTL of at most 604,800 s (1 week).
Memory cross-references are auto-detected from $memory.set()/$memory.get() calls.
Validation and compilation never execute content.
Success and error edges ignore sourceHandle and preserve stored candidate order.
Only exact memoryVersion v2 selects V2 memory; absent and other strings use the V1 fallback.
A script failure is reported through codeResponse.error and routed to the failed edge (code/index.ts:91-99); it is not an execution crash.

The script can write into the execution context: prepareOutputData merges codeResponse.context and codeResponse.output over execData (code/index.ts:101, 131-134). Later nodes may read what this node wrote.
Success and node errors are routed by the fixed node-type switch (workflow-engine.service.ts:1853-1869): an error response follows the failed edge instead of crashing the execution.

The router has no specific selection for this type: selectNodeTypeRouting returns every candidate edge through default: return { edges } (legacy-routing-selector.ts:131-153), so sourceHandle is ignored and all connected edges fan out in stored order.
Runtime resources, templates, and side effects are never resolved or executed by workflow-core.
Precondition: Execution-time policy, secrets, and resource access are authorized outside workflow-core.

rules: Never write a START node. The tool adds the workflow's one START (`validate --fix` and `jelou push` write it), unless the workflow enters only through a WEBHOOK.
Your first edge is { "sourceId": "START", "targetId": "<first-node>", "branch": "default" }. "START" is a reserved alias the tool resolves to the real START id; no other node may use that id.
The first node cannot be START, WEBHOOK, EMPTY, NOTE.
WEBHOOK is optional, at most one per workflow, and never chained to START.

A workflow or tool that enters only through a WEBHOOK needs no START: write no edge from "START" and the tool adds none. A channel message or a TOOL node never starts it then. A marketplace skill always needs START.
Next to a wired WEBHOOK that feeds the flow, a START with no edge is only a warning: the tool wires nothing to it and push keeps it.
